Messages.Author: Dave the Romantic
Messages.Body:
From my friend Bill:

"I have been hearing contradictory reports as to rulings on a couple of
Serpentis cards. Can you or can you not choose one of your own vampires as the
target of a Temptation? If you can, can the acting vampire target himself?
Also, I've heard that Heart of Darkness has been amended to only change
aggravated damage dealt in combat, (i.e., it will not alter damage from Daring
the Dawn nor from Rutor's Hand.) Is this true? Have similar rulings been made
for Armor of Terra or Concordance?
Thanks much!"

Thanks,
Bill

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Dave the Romantic wrote:
> From my friend Bill:
>
> "I have been hearing contradictory reports as to rulings on a couple of
> Serpentis cards. Can you or can you not choose one of your own vampires as the
> target of a Temptation? If you can, can the acting vampire target himself?

Can. Yes.

> Also, I've heard that Heart of Darkness has been amended to only change
> aggravated damage dealt in combat, (i.e., it will not alter damage from Daring
> the Dawn nor from Rutor's Hand.) Is this true? Have similar rulings been made
> for Armor of Terra or Concordance?

It is not true.
Card text is used in all those cases.

For Bill's future reference (towards a speedier answer), the current
rulings and errata are available online, as is a list of all card text
migrations.

http://www.white-wolf.com/vtes/Rules.html
